questions.question: By default, how does useSelector decide whether a component should re-render after an action?
options: It deep-compares the entire root state
It compares the new selector result with the previous one using ===
It re-renders every subscribed component on every dispatch
It checks whether the action type mentions the component's slice
questions.explanation: When state changes, the selector re-runs and its result is compared by reference (===). Only a different result triggers a re-render.

questions.question: `useSelector((s) => s.cart.items.map((i) => i.name))` re-renders the component when an unrelated slice changes. Why?
options: map() returns a new array each time, so the === check fails
The cart slice is mutated by the other reducer
Provider re-renders all children on every state change
questions.explanation: Any change to root state re-runs the selector. Returning a new array reference makes === fail even when contents are equal. Select existing references, use shallowEqual, or memoise.

questions.question: Which statement about the function returned by useDispatch is correct?
options: It changes on every render, so it must be wrapped in useCallback
It can only dispatch actions created by createSlice
It must be called during render to be batched
It is the store's dispatch, so its reference is stable and safe in effect dependencies
questions.explanation: useDispatch returns store.dispatch, which never changes for a given store. Dispatch in event handlers and effects, not during render.

questions.question: A component reads `useStore().getState().user.name` during render. What is the problem?
options: useStore throws outside of class components
getState() returns a frozen copy that cannot be read
Reading the store this way does not subscribe the component, so it can show stale data
It causes the component to re-render on every action
questions.explanation: Only useSelector subscribes to store updates. Reading getState() in render gives a one-off snapshot that will not update when the user changes.
